setting.note: A man called only K. arrives in a snowbound village to take up work as a land-surveyor, and spends the book trying and failing to reach the Castle on the hill that supposedly summoned him, its offices always one message further away.

rights.originalWork: In copyright through much of the 20th century; Franz Kafka wrote it in 1922 and left it unfinished, published posthumously in 1926. This book is mapped as a cited work: we store none of its text and reproduce no passages. The places are facts and the notes are our own.
rights.translation: Originally written in German (Das Schloss). The descriptions here are our own English words, not a quotation of any translation.
rights.textSource: None stored. A cited book reproduces no text.
rights.territoryNotes: Locations and original commentary only. No reproduction of the copyrighted text, in any territory.
